asker_query: Sister, I want to prepare for my last days — I will not go to ICU, I will stay at home, I have to prepare some papers for my wife, I have things to say to my son. But whenever I raise the topic, my wife cries, my son stops me saying 'don't talk like this'. How can you help me?
answer:
It is deeply distressing to be unable to discuss your final wishes with your loved ones.
Always ensure you continue your laxatives (like Senna) and anti-emetics, as these are essential to manage the side effects of strong opioids.
To bridge the gap with your family, we must move toward "individualized care." As a caregiver or health worker, I can act as a neutral facilitator to help your family understand that discussing your wishes is not "giving up," but rather a way to ensure your dignity and reduce their future uncertainty.
We can schedule a quiet, calm time to sit with your wife and son, where I will help explain that your desire to prepare these papers is a way to protect them and honor your relationship.
We will document your preferred place of care—your home—and your specific wishes, ensuring that your family feels supported rather than abandoned.
If you feel your pain is becoming unmanageable or if you experience new, distressing symptoms, this is a red-flag trigger to contact your palliative care team immediately for an urgent review.
Beyond medication, we can employ non-pharmacological comfort measures to help you feel more at peace.
Simple actions like propping yourself up with pillows, ensuring good ventilation, or using relaxation techniques—such as focusing on happy memories or listening to favorite music—can significantly improve your quality of life.

_(The specific amount and schedule of any medicine are not included here. Take that part of your question to your next consultation.)_
